name: Manifold n-diagram (informal statement)
quote: A manifold n-diagram is a framed conical tame stratification of the open n-cube.

name: Tame m-tangle in dimension n (informal statement)
quote: A tame m-tangle in dimension n is an m-manifold tamely embedded in the open n-cube which is framed transversal.

name: Combinatorialization of manifold diagrams and tame tangles (Theorem 3, informal)
quote: Manifold diagrams up to framed stratified homeomorphism are classified by combinatorial manifold diagrams.

name: Stable tangle singularities dim <= 4 (Theorem 5)

data.case1: one stable 1-tangle singularity in dim 2 and dim 3

quote: There are three stable 2-tangle singularities in dim 3: these are shown in Fig. I.5.

name: Manifold diagrams dualize to cell diagrams (Observation 4)
quote: Up to framed stratified homeomorphism, manifold and cell diagrams are in correspondence by geometric dualization.

name: Entrance path preorder / stratification

data.Entr(f): preorder on strata, arrows s->r for nonempty intersections

quote: Its entrance path preorder Entr(f) is the preorder whose objects are strata s, and whose arrows are generated by arrows s to r.

name: n-Framed space

data.n-framed chart: embedding gamma: U -> R^n of subspace U of X
data.framed map: F framed on charts if pi_{>i} rho F = F_i pi_{>i} gamma for all i
data.framed compatible: identity is framed map on overlap of two charts
data.n-framing structure: atlas of framed compatible charts covering X

equations: pi_{>i} ∘ ρ ∘ F = F_i ∘ pi_{>i} ∘ γ
quote: An 'n-framed chart' (U, γ) in X is an embedding γ : U ,→ Rn of a subspace U ⊂ X.

name: Categorical directions of R^n

data.k-arrow: arrow with k parallel lines, points in kth categorical direction

quote: We refer to the (n − k)th coordinate of Rn as its 'kth categorical direction'.

name: Tame stratification (framed stratification)

data.condition: stratification (X,f) that has a mesh refinement M -> f

quote: A tame stratification (X, f, γ) is a stratification (X, f) of a flat framed space (X, γ) that has a mesh refinement.

name: Coarsest refining meshes (Theorem 1.4.16)

data.claim: every tame stratification has a unique coarsest refining mesh

quote: Every tame stratification f has a unique 'coarsest refining mesh' M, satisfying that any other mesh refinement factors through it.

name: Combinatorialization of tame stratifications (Theorem 1.4.24)

data.correspondence: tame stratifications up to framed stratified homeomorphism <-> normalized stratified trusses

quote: Tame stratifications up to framed stratified homeomorphism are in 1-to-1 correspondence with normalized stratified trusses.

name: 1-Mesh
quote: A 1-mesh M is a stratified framed contractible 0- or 1-manifold, whose strata are open 0- or 1-disks.

name: 1-Mesh bundle

data.coordinatizability: bundle embedding gamma: M -> B x R restricting fiberwise
data.0-constructibility: fiber-dim-0 strata lift entrance paths uniquely

quote: A 1-mesh bundle p : M → B is a stratified bundle together with a choice of 1-mesh structure Mb for each stratified fiber.

name: n-Mesh

data.structure: tower of 1-mesh bundles p_n: M_n -> M_{n-1} -> ... -> M_1 -> M_0 = *

quote: An n-mesh M is a tower of 1-mesh bundles Mn → Mn−1 → ... → M1 → M0 = ∗.

name: n-Mesh bundle

data.structure: tower of 1-mesh bundles p_i: M_i -> M_{i-1}, 1<=i<=n, M_0=B

quote: An n-mesh bundle p over a 'base' stratification B is a tower of 1-mesh bundles.

name: Frame order in meshes

data.definition: s ≺ t iff gamma(s) < gamma(t) for coordinatization gamma: M -> R

quote: Given a 1-mesh M and strata s, t in M, we write s ≺ t if for some coordinatization γ we have γ(s) < γ(t).

name: 1-Truss

data.classifying mesh: M with Entr(M) ≅ T compatible with dim and ≺

quote: A 1-truss T = (T, ≤, dim, ≺) is a poset (T, ≤) together with a 'dimension' map dim and a 'frame order'.

name: n-Truss

data.structure: tower of 1-truss bundles T_n -> T_{n-1} -> ... -> T_1 -> T_0 = *
data.role: combinatorial dual/counterpart of n-mesh (structured entrance path poset)

quote: An n-truss T is a tower of 1-truss bundles Tn → Tn−1 → ... → T1 → T0 = ∗.

name: Cell dimension of an n-truss object
quote: We define dim(x) := Σ dimi(x) and speak of that sum as the 'cell dimension' of x.

name: n-Truss bordism category T_n

data.construction: n-fold application of T_1(-) to terminal category
data.role: classifies n-truss bundles: bundles over P correspond to functors P -> T_n

quote: The category of n-trusses and their bordisms Tn is the category obtained by n times applying the functor T1(−) to the terminal category ∗.

name: Truss dualization functor

data.action: T = {pi: Ti -> Ti-1} maps to T† = {pi†: Ti^op -> Ti-1^op}

quote: The truss dualization † : Trsn → Trsn takes n-trusses T to their dual n-trusses T†.

name: Mesh-truss duality (equivalence of meshes and trusses)
quote: The functors FTrs : M̄eshn → T̄rsn and FTrs : M̊eshn → T̊rsn are weak equivalences of ∞-categories.

name: Dualization of n-meshes (Corollary 1.4.6)
quote: There is an ∞-functor † : M̄eshn ≃ M̊eshn determined by requiring FTrs ◦ † = † ◦ FTrs.

name: Framed conical stratification
quote: f is (tame) framed conical at x if there is a (tame) link and a (tame) framed stratified neighborhood φ: Ik × (In−k, c(lx)) ,→ (In, f).

name: Manifold n-diagram

data.strata: k-manifolds locally homeomorphic to I^k via projection I^n -> I^k

quote: A manifold n-diagram (In, f) is a tame stratification of the open cube that is tame framed conical.

name: Combinatorial manifold diagram
quote: A combinatorial manifold n-diagram (also called a 'manifold diagram n-truss') is a normalized open stratified n-truss (T,f) that is combinatorially conical.

name: Combinatorialization of manifold diagrams (Theorem 2.3.3)

data.correspondence: framed stratified homeo classes of manifold n-diagrams <-> combinatorial manifold n-diagrams

quote: Framed stratified homeomorphism classes of manifold n-diagrams are in 1-to-1 correspondence with combinatorial manifold n-diagrams.

name: Cell diagram

data.condition: tame stratification dual to a manifold n-diagram
data.combinatorial dual: combinatorial cell diagram = normalized closed stratified n-truss that is combinatorially facetal

quote: A cell n-diagram (X, f) is a tame stratification that is dual to a manifold n-diagram.

name: Pasting-diagram reading of cell diagrams
quote: Cell diagrams can be depicted as classical 'point and arrow diagrams' by replacing k-cells by k-arrows if they are non-degenerate, and by 'k-identities' if they are degenerate.

name: Framed transversality (tameness condition for tangles)

data.m-transversal: x has tame framed neighborhood Im x (In-m, ce(l)) with l empty link
data.k-transversal (k<m): x has framed neighborhood Ik x (In-k, ce(l)) with l=(S^{m-k-1} -> ∂I^{n-k}) tame link, and off-cone points are j-transversal for j>k
data.tame framed transversal stratification: all points x in W are kx-transversal for some kx

quote: We say f is a tame framed transversal stratification if all points x ∈ W are kx-transversal points of W for some 0 ≤ kx ≤ m.

name: Tame tangle
quote: A tame m-tangle f = (W ,→ In) is a tame embedded m-manifold such that f is a tame framed transversal stratification.

name: Combinatorial transversality

data.subposet: D ↪ Cn-k containing cone point, D \ > an (m-k-1)-sphere

quote: A stratified open n-truss (T, f: Q ,→ Tn) is said to be combinatorially m-dim k-transversal at x if there exists an open cone (n − k)-truss C.

name: Tangle truss (combinatorial tangle)
quote: An m-tangle n-truss (T, f : Q ,→ Tn), is a normalized stratified open n-truss that is combinatorially m-dim transversal.

name: Combinatorializing tame tangles (Theorem 3.1.25)

data.correspondence: framed stratified homeo classes of tame m-tangles in In <-> m-tangle n-trusses

quote: Framed stratified homeomorphism classes of tame m-tangles in In are in 1-to-1 correspondence with m-tangle n-trusses.

name: Tangles refine to manifold diagrams (Theorem 3.1.32)

data.refinement: transversal stratification tstr(f) of a tame tangle

quote: Given a tame tangle f, then the transversal stratification tstr(f) of the tangle is a manifold diagram.

name: Tangle singularity (m-singularity)

data.condition: m-tangle n-truss (T,f) where T is an open cone truss

quote: An m-tangle n-truss (T, f) is called an m-singularity if T is an open cone truss.

name: Stability of a singularity

data.condition: no perturbation (T,f) ⇝ (S,g) exists with #Q > #W≤x for all x in W

quote: An m-singularity (T, f : Q ,→ Tn) is stable if there exists no perturbation (T, f) * (S, g : W ,→ Sn) such that for all x ∈ W we have #Q > #W≤x.

name: F-equivalence (framed isotopy)

data.condition: stable singularities joined by a path (T,f) -> (S,g)

quote: Stable singularities (T, f) and (S, g) are said to be F-equivalent (or 'framed isotopic'), written (T, f) ≃F (S, g), if there is a path (T, f) → (S, f).

name: Basic tangle singularities up to ambient dimension 2
quote: there is a single 0-tangle singularities in dimension 1... there are two 1-tangle singularities in dimension 2... there is also a single 0-tangle singularity in dimension 2.

name: Extrema singularity
quote: The three singularities in Fig. I.5 will be called 'extrema', 'saddles', and 'cusps' respectively.

name: Saddle singularity
quote: extrema and saddles together as the A2d1 singularities.

name: Cusp singularity
quote: the cusps as the A2 singularities.

name: Stable 2-tangle singularities in dim 3 (Proposition 3.3.2)

data.count: three, up to reflection and F-equivalence

quote: Up to reflection and F-equivalence, there are three stable 2-singularities in I3, namely, those depicted in Fig. I.5.

name: A1-oplus singularity

data.link: 0-sphere (two points), one in source and one in target 2-cube

quote: Up to F-equivalence and reflection, there is one stable 1-tangle singularity in I3: namely, the singularity depicted (together with its reflection) in Fig. 3.23.

name: Stable 1-tangle singularities in dim 3 (Proposition 3.3.6)

data.count: one, up to F-equivalence and reflection
data.name: A1⊕

quote: Up to F-equivalence and reflection, there is one stable 1-tangle singularity in I3.

name: Braid-trivializing singularity

data.origin: braiding of points in the plane provides its link

quote: the ability to braid points in the plane provides the link of a new singularity which trivializes the braid; this singularity is depicted in Fig. 3.26.

name: Stable 2-tangle singularities in dim 4 (Proposition 3.3.7)

data.count: four, up to reflection and F-equivalence
data.composition: three stabilized from dim 3 + one new braid-trivializing singularity

quote: Up to reflection and F-equivalence, there are four stable 2-singularities in I4, namely, those depicted in Fig. 3.25 and Fig. 3.26.

name: D2 singularity class

data.origin: identification of two coinciding classes A2⇔(3,1)A2d1 and A1⇔2A2

quote: we jointly denote the classes of singularities (A2 ⇔(3,1) A2d1) and (A1 ⇔3 A2) by D2.

name: D3 singularity (relator)

data.type: triple binary relator of D2 singularities in A2-shape

quote: D3 is the first example of such a 'triple binary relator'.

name: D4 / elliptic umbilic singularity

data.perturbation: admits perturbation to a binary relator of D3 singularities

quote: for the D4 singularity (which in Thom's classification is also known as the 'elliptic umbilic singularity'), the question is answered positively in this section.

name: 3-tangle singularities in dim 4 (Remark 3.3.9)
quote: We claim that there are nine classes of stable singularities in this case ... which can be reasonably organized into five 'types' of singularities.

name: ADE classification of R-simple R-orbits (Arnold)

data.Thom_seven: A2, A3, A4, A5, D4±, D5 (up to codimension 5)

quote: Thom's original seven 'elementary singularities' exactly describe those orbits up to codimension 5, which are A2, A3, A4, A5, D4±, and D5.

name: Morse and Morse-Cerf singularity counterparts
quote: The counterpart of A2d1 are the 'Morse singularities' f(x1,x2)=±x1^2±x2^2 ... The counterpart of A2 are the 'Morse-Cerf singularities' f(x1,u1)=±x1^3±u1x1.

name: Projecting 2-tangles (drawing convention)

data.method: project non-regular points (transversal dimension < 2) along I3 -> I2
data.coloring: deformation between sampled slices shown in color
data.disambiguation: initial condition given by a full 2-tangle picture in I3

quote: we often depict 2-tangles in I3 by the projections of their 'non-regular points' along I3 → I2.

name: Combinatorialization of smooth structures (Hypothesis 6)

data.claim: smooth structures on manifolds can be captured by tame tangles up to framed stratified homeomorphisms

quote: Smooth structures on manifolds can be captured by tame tangles up to framed stratified homeomorphisms.

name: Coordinatizing open n-meshes

data.coordinatization: gamma: M -> R^n with image the open cube I^n = (-1,1)^n

quote: Any open n-mesh M has a coordinatization γ : M ,→ Rn whose image is the open cube In = (−1, 1)n ⊂ Rn.
